transcript_tail.text: I'll investigate what's available — both the skills and the remote-control mechanisms in this repo — before answering.

Short answer: **there's no skill that broadcasts "resume" to all sessions at once** — and right now there's nothing resumable to broadcast to anyway. Here's the full picture:

## What exists for resuming

| Mechanism | Scope | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `usage-limit-monitor.py` (daemon, **running** as pid 1352) | Auto, all usage-limit-paused sessions | Detects sessions stuck on the cloud usage limit and runs `claude --resume <sid> -p continue`, **one at a time**, oldest first, with 5/15/30-min backoff |
| `/resume-work` skill | One session, interactive | Lists recent/interrupted sessions, you pick one, it reconstructs the goal and continues |
| `/session-triage` skill | Per-repo, read-only | Finds sessions that hit API failures / ended mid-task and emits resume prompts — but doesn't fire the resumes |

So "all sessions resume" is already a thing for the **usage-limit** case — by design it's a steady drip, not a broadcast, specifically to avoid one mass-resume immediately re-tripping the org limit. There is no skill (and the README explicitly notes the remote-control *server* has no resume) for waking every live session.

## Why there's nothing to resume right now

The monitor is tracking exactly **one** paused session, and it's a dead end:

```
sid=897c7901-…  cwd=…/FamilyFund/.claude/worktrees/…/app1
17 attempts, every one: rc=1 "No conversation found with session ID: 897c7901-…"
```

That conversation no longer exists on disk (worktree likely merged/cleaned), so `--resume` can never succeed. The monitor will keep retrying every 30 min until the 7-day GC drops it on **~2026-05-28**.

## So, your options

- **Nothing to do** — the only auto-resumable session is the unresumable ghost above; no real work is paused.
- **Stop the wasted retries** — I can tombstone `897c7901…` in `logs/paused-sessions.json` (set `resumed_at`) so the monitor quits hammering a session that's gone.
- **Resume a *specific* interrupted chat** — run `/resume-work` (it'll list candidates per repo).

Want me to tombstone the dead session, or were you thinking of a different set of sessions (e.g. interrupted-mid-task rather than usage-limit-paused)?

Good — that's a different and more important case than what I was looking at. Those are live cloud sessions parked at "Usage limit reached / Try again," and the monitor is only tracking one ghost session. Let me find out why these aren't being detected.

The only local match is *this very conversation's* transcript (it matched because I typed "review-unused-controllers" here). That's the key clue. Let me confirm whether the screenshot session even exists locally, and check the recent FamilyFund worktrees/transcripts.

That confirms it. Here's what's actually going on — and it's not good news for automating those:

## The sessions in your screenshot are **cloud-hosted**, not local

The clues all line up:
- The session says *"This is a Debian container with PHP 8.4… I can install MariaDB server locally"* — that's an Anthropic **cloud sandbox**, not your Mac (which is Darwin and uses the FamilyFund `lease-env`/`test-env` pools, never "install MariaDB in a Debian container").
- No local worktree, no local branch `review-unused-controllers-vLL1Q` / `vLL1Q`, and no local transcript for it. The only file that even matched "review-unused-controllers" was *this* chat's own transcript.

So those PR #11 sessions run in the cloud, and their transcripts never touch `~/.claude/projects/`.

## Why nothing here can resume them

| Tool | Sees cloud sessions? |
|---|---|
| `usage-limit-monitor.py` daemon | ❌ Only scans local `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`. Its one tracked entry is a local ghost. |
| `/resume-work`, `/session-triage` skills | ❌ Same — local transcripts only. |
| RemoteTrigger API (the only cloud surface I have) | ❌ It's for scheduled *routines* (new runs), not resuming a paused conversation. List is empty anyway. |

**So: no — there's no skill and no command I can run to tell those sessions to "Try again."** That button is cloud-side state. Practically, you either click "Try again" per session in the app, or wait for your limit to reset (some will continue on their own when you re-engage). There's no "resume all" in the cloud product surfaced to this environment.

## Two things worth flagging

1. **The whole local auto-resume design doesn't cover your real pain.** It was built and "verified" against *local* remote-control workers, but your actual usage-limit pileups are **cloud** sessions it structurally can't touch. That's a meaningful gap vs. the README's "usage-limit auto-resume monitor" framing.

2. **Even for local sessions there's a detection hole:** the monitor only inspects the **last line** of each transcript. Recent FamilyFund transcripts end with a `type: ai-title` entry — if any non-error line lands after the 429, the session reads as "not paused" and gets skipped. (Moot for the screenshot, but a real bug for the local case.)

Where do you want to go from here?
